title: Solar storms around a black hole
desc:
Researchers from the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology have discovered evidence that powerful eruptions near supermassive black holes are driven by the same physical processes responsible for solar storms. The findings, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, provide new insights into the behavior of matter and magnetic fields in the extreme environments surrounding black holes.
The international research team, led by doctoral student Gal Vardi under the supervision of Prof. Ehud Behar of the Technion Faculty of Physics, studied X-ray emissions from the supermassive black hole at the center of the galaxy NGC 3783. Using observations from the XRISM and XMM-Newton space telescopes, the researchers identified the “Neupert effect,” a phenomenon first observed on the Sun in 1968 but never previously detected around a black hole.
The discovery provides evidence that magnetic reconnection – the process in which magnetic energy is released and converted into other forms of energy – can trigger powerful eruptions and coronal mass ejections near black holes, just as it does on the Sun. The findings reveal a remarkable connection between solar activity and the behavior of some of the most extreme objects in the universe, advancing our understanding of the physical mechanisms governing these cosmic environments.
